item.text:
Continuation completed for Chapters 2B–8B. No scores were assigned. New IDs are provisional because the read-only workspace prevented manifest persistence; numbering continues from RC027.

### 2B — Conflict, peace, and protection

- **RC028** — Indonesia’s presidential statement on Myanmar required implementation of the ASEAN Five-Point Consensus, access for the special envoy, inclusive dialogue, and nondiscriminatory aid (21 Jan. 2022, Cabinet Secretariat, paras. 46–57). Direct presidential attribution; efficacy unverified. **Lenses:** 2B.1, 2B.5, 2B.7, 2B.10. [Source](https://setkab.go.id/presiden-jokowi-kembali-tegaskan-pentingnya-implementasi-lima-butir-konsensus-asean-untuk-masalah-myanmar/)

- **RC029** — Indonesian Foreign Ministry reported no significant Myanmar 5PC progress after one year and urged prompt access for the envoy (1 Feb. 2022, ANTARA, paras. 63–69). Contrary efficacy evidence. **Lenses:** 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10. [Source](https://en.antaranews.com/news/212769/indonesia-urges-myanmar-military-to-promptly-implement-aseans-5pc)

- **RC030** — RSIS assessed ASEAN’s 2022 Myanmar approach as under pressure from continuing brutality and executions, arguing that barring junta participation remained insufficient without stronger consequences (22 Sept. 2022, executive summary). Independent analytical contrary evidence. **Lenses:** 2B.1, 2B.7, 2B.10. [Source](https://rsis.edu.sg/staff-publication/asean-and-the-five-point-consensus-on-myanmar-a-futile-exercise/)

- **RC031** — Komnas HAM stated that Papua special autonomy had not fully delivered human rights, public services, or welfare, and called for measurable oversight of special-autonomy funds and institutional conflict handling (15 Feb. 2022, paras. 80–89). National institutional evidence; not personal blame. **Lenses:** 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.9, 2B.10. [Source](https://www.komnasham.go.id/index.php/news/2022/2/15/2081/komnas-ham-otsus-untuk-kesejahteraan-orang-asli-papua.html)

- **RC032** — Indonesia’s 2022 UN response documented police/ICRC training on international use-of-force standards and stated that ICRC had helped draft military SOPs and rules of engagement; it also defended access restrictions as security-based (UN document, pp. 7–10). Official contrary account, not independent efficacy proof. **Lenses:** 2B.4, 2B.5, 2B.9. [Source](https://spcommreports.ohchr.org/TMResultsBase/DownLoadFile?gId=36826)

### 3B — Human rights

- **RC033** — The U.S. 2022 report recorded abuses by security forces, harsh prison conditions, arbitrary detention, Papua abuses, restrictions on expression and assembly, and weak accountability (sections 1–2). External official finding with attribution limits. **Lenses:** 3B.1–3B.10. [Source](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089237.html)

- **RC034** — The same report stated that civilian authorities retained control over police and armed forces, while investigations and prosecutions occurred in some cases but impunity remained significant (paras. 37–41). Contrary/contextual attribution evidence. **Lenses:** 3B.1, 3B.9, 3B.10.

- **RC035** — Human Rights Monitor reported that Papua police and military violations were rarely processed and that internal accountability mechanisms lacked transparency and independence (2022 annual report, paras. 43–49). Adverse remedy evidence. **Lenses:** 3B.1, 3B.4, 3B.9, 3B.10. [Source](https://humanrightsmonitor.org/reports/west-papua-2022/)

- **RC036** — Human Rights Monitor recorded 43 civilian deaths in Papua conflict in 2022, including deaths attributed to both security forces and TPNPB, preserving contested responsibility rather than assigning it automatically to Widodo (paras. 61–83). Event-level contrary evidence. **Lenses:** 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.9.

- **RC037** — The 2022 Paniai human-rights trial acquitted the sole defendant; judges found insufficient proof of command responsibility, while dissenting judges and observers argued that higher command responsibility required further investigation (paras. 124–133). Adverse accountability evidence with explicit legal uncertainty. **Lenses:** 3B.1, 3B.9, 3B.10.

- **RC038** — Widodo issued Presidential Decree 17/2022 creating a team for non-judicial settlement of twelve historic abuses, including restitution recommendations; victims and monitors criticized the process as rushed and potentially substituting for judicial accountability (22 Dec. 2022, paras. 45–68). Direct formal action plus contrary evidence. **Lenses:** 3B.9, 3B.10. [Source](https://humanrightsmonitor.org/news/victims-and-relatives-disappointed-over-settlement-of-serious-human-rights-violations-in-indonesia/)

- **RC039** — Komnas Perempuan maintained a 2022 decision documenting discriminatory policy based on sexual orientation; the page was discoverable but not retrievable in full, so it remains **discovery_only**, not final evidence. **Lenses:** 3B.5, 3B.7.

### 4B — Democratic institutions

- **RC040** — Widodo chaired a limited meeting on the Criminal Code bill; the government described civil-society participation and changes to provisions on death penalty, defamation, and the ITE law (28 Nov. 2022, paras. 37–48). Direct executive legislative involvement. **Lenses:** 4B.2, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7. [Source](https://setkab.go.id/en/president-jokowi-chairs-limited-meeting-on-criminal-code-bill/)

- **RC041** — The Library of Congress reported that the Criminal Code would require implementation regulations and guidelines before taking effect, limiting the evidence to enactment and intended implementation rather than 2022 enforcement (11 Dec. 2022, paras. 40–67). Precise temporal and implementation constraint. **Lenses:** 4B.2, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.10. [Source](https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2022-12-11/indonesia-new-criminal-code-passed-by-parliament/)

- **RC042** — The same analysis recorded criticism that the Code threatened women, minorities, LGBT people, speech, and association, while noting that judicial review remained available but trust in the Constitutional Court had weakened. Contrary institutional evidence. **Lenses:** 4B.3, 4B.7, 4B.9.

- **RC043** — The Presidential Staff Office characterized the Criminal Code as a presidential legacy and promised a three-year public and law-enforcement education period while stating that criticism would remain permissible (14 Dec. 2022, paras. 76–87). Official favorable claim; efficacy unverified. **Lenses:** 4B.2, 4B.3, 4B.6. [Source](https://www.ksp.go.id/moeldoko-kuhp-bukan-untuk-kepentingan-pemerintah-saat-ini.html)

- **RC044** — Freedom House recorded a largely democratic electoral framework and mostly impartial election authorities, but noted that mandatory KPU/Bawaslu consultation with parliament and government could reduce electoral independence (2022 report, paras. 92–107). Balanced favorable/adverse institutional evidence. **Lenses:** 4B.1, 4B.4, 4B.8. [Source](https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-world/2022)

- **RC045** — Freedom House reported continued political pluralism and peaceful transfers of power, alongside military influence, online propaganda, corruption, and government pressure on universities and media (paras. 112–164, 179). Contrary and balancing context; some incidents predate 2022. **Lenses:** 4B.1, 4B.3, 4B.4, 4B.9.

### 5B — Economic management

- **RC046** — The World Bank approved a $750 million fiscal-reform loan to raise revenue, improve tax equity, strengthen subnational fiscal transfers, and improve budget execution (24 June 2022, paras. 143–151). Formal policy action; outcomes unverified. **Lenses:** 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.5, 5B.6, 5B.7. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2022/06/24/new-support-will-help-strengthen-indonesia-tax-system-improve-development-spending)

- **RC047** — The World Bank identified low tax revenue, weak public-investment spending, and post-COVID fiscal constraints as barriers to inclusive growth (same source, paras. 143–150). Independent adverse implementation context. **Lenses:** 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.9, 5B.10.

- **RC048** — BPK reported that its 2022 review covered 137 central-government financial audits, 41 performance audits, and 48 special-purpose audits, including poverty reduction, subsidies, and public-service obligations (1 Nov. 2022, paras. 53–58). Independent audit-system evidence. **Lenses:** 5B.5, 5B.7, 5B.10. [Source](https://www.bpk.go.id/news/bpk-serahkan-ikhtisar-hasil-pemeriksaan-semester-i-tahun-2022-kepada-presiden)

- **RC049** — World Bank’s 2022 poverty brief reported poverty falling to 9.5% in March 2022 and social-assistance coverage reaching 97.2%, but identified high inclusion and exclusion errors and stagnant inequality (pp. 1–2). Outcome plus distributional shortfall. **Lenses:** 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9, 5B.10. [Source](https://databankfiles.worldbank.org/public/ddpext_download/poverty/987B9C90-CB9F-4D93-AE8C-750588BF00QA/current/Global_POVEQ_IDN.pdf)

- **RC050** — The World Bank recorded 98% distribution of designated basic-needs transfers in Q1 2022, but warned that targeting errors persisted and that fuel-price increases could worsen inflation and poverty (p. 1). Balanced delivery evidence. **Lenses:** 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10.

- **RC051** — The December 2022 Economic Prospects report projected 5.2% growth but attributed recovery materially to reopening and exceptionally favorable terms of trade, limiting ruler-specific attribution (pp. 40–41). Contrary attribution evidence. **Lenses:** 5B.1, 5B.9, 5B.10. [Source](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099440012142242417/pdf/P1795560cfe1930180bb46080253f7faa21.pdf)

### 6B — Human development

- **RC052** — World Bank technical discussions with Indonesia supported learning-recovery frameworks, hybrid learning, and psychosocial support as schools reopened for the 2022 academic year. **Lenses:** 6B.2, 6B.5, 6B.6, 6B.9. [Source](https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/eastasiapacific/recovering-impacts-covid-19-school-closures-indonesia)

- **RC053** — The World Bank estimated 0.9–1.2 years of learning loss and continued school closures into early 2022, establishing a major target-period shock rather than a standalone ruler finding. **Lenses:** 6B.2, 6B.5, 6B.6, 6B.10. [Source](https://blogs.worldbank.org/en/eastasiapacific/recovering-impacts-covid-19-school-closures-indonesia)

- **RC054** — World Bank analysis documented government mitigation through emergency curricula, educational television, and subsidized internet quotas. Favorable response evidence; effectiveness not independently established. **Lenses:** 6B.2, 6B.5, 6B.6. [Source](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/estimates-of-covid-19-impacts-on-learning-and-earning-in-indonesia-how-to-turn-the-tide)

- **RC055** — A 2022 Indonesian study of social protection and stunting warned that cross-sectional data could not establish causality and called for evaluation of benefit continuity, adequacy, targeting, and coordination. Independent methodological limitation. **Lenses:** 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.6, 6B.10. [Source](https://e-journal.unair.ac.id/JAKI/article/view/77680)

- **RC056** — A study of pandemic-era stunting prevention identified limited health personnel, weak measurement calibration, and monitoring constraints as implementation problems. **Lenses:** 6B.3, 6B.5, 6B.6, 6B.9. [Source](https://ejournal.undip.ac.id/index.php/jmki/article/view/42792)

- **RC057** — World Bank project documentation identifies equitable health-service utilization and quality improvement as a continuing reform objective, confirming policy alignment but not realized regional quality or affordability. **Lenses:** 6B.1, 6B.3, 6B.4, 6B.9.

### 7B — Integrity

- **RC058** — Jokowi’s LHKPN for the 2022 period reported assets of Rp82.37 billion, up approximately Rp10.90 billion from the prior report, with no reported debt. This is a disclosure record, not proof of honesty or concealment. **Lenses:** 7B.1, 7B.2, 7B.3. [Source](https://www.kompas.com/tren/read/2023/04/11/090000065/harta-kekayaan-jokowi-naik-rp-10-miliar-selama-2022-ini-rinciannya)

- **RC059** — The disclosure listed land/buildings, vehicles, movable assets, and cash, providing a recoverable primary-data target for later beneficial-ownership comparison. **Lenses:** 7B.1, 7B.2, 7B.4.

- **RC060** — Widodo publicly called for legal reform and asked parties to follow the KPK process (26 Sept. 2022). Direct favorable safeguard evidence; no independent test of implementation. **Lenses:** 7B.6, 7B.7. [Source](https://setkab.go.id/presiden-tegaskan-urgensi-reformasi-hukum-di-indonesia/)

- **RC061** — BPK reported a performance audit concerning governance, action-setting, and monitoring of Indonesia’s national anti-corruption strategy for 2019–2022. Institutional accountability evidence; not personal integrity evidence. **Lenses:** 7B.6, 7B.7, 7B.10. [Source](https://www.bpk.go.id/news/selesaikan-pemeriksaan-bpk-serahkan-lhp-atas-lk-kpk-tahun-2022)

- **RC062** — Indonesia Corruption Watch was reported as holding Widodo and parliament responsible for declining public trust in KPK after institutional weakening. This is an attributed civil-society allegation, not an adjudicated personal finding. **Lenses:** 7B.6, 7B.7. [Source](https://www.thejakartapost.com/paper/2022/04/06/president-house-responsible-for-waning-trust-in-kpk.html)

- **RC063** — Searches found no target-period verified evidence of Widodo’s personal enrichment, family benefit, beneficial-ownership concealment, or direct obstruction. This remains `unresolved`, not adverse evidence.

### 8B — Effectiveness

- **RC064** — Indonesia’s PEN program had disbursed Rp29.3 trillion, or 6.4% of its 2022 allocation, by 1 April under a meeting chaired by Widodo. Direct implementation evidence with limited early-year coverage. **Lenses:** 8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.5. [Source](https://setkab.go.id/hingga-1-april-realisasi-program-pemulihan-ekonomi-nasional-2022-capai-rp293-triliun/)

- **RC065** — World Bank’s village-service implementation record provides a 30 June 2022 monitoring point for institutional strengthening and village service delivery, but does not establish national-scale effectiveness or presidential ownership. **Lenses:** 8B.2, 8B.4, 8B.7. [Source](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099715106302221571)

- **RC066** — The World Bank’s independent evaluation later identified capacity gains in local governments and water utilities but lagging urban and subnational infrastructure projects because of weak local capacity. Retrospective evaluation of programs active during the period; contrary implementation evidence. **Lenses:** 8B.2, 8B.4, 8B.7. [Source](https://ieg.worldbankgroup.org/evaluations/world-bank-group-indonesia)

- **RC067** — The G20 communiqué was achieved despite deep disagreement over Ukraine; most members condemned the invasion, while “different assessments” remained. This supports a diplomatic process outcome, not conflict resolution. **Lenses:** 8B.1, 8B.9. [Source](https://www.axios.com/2022/11/16/g20-communique-condemn-russia-invasion)

- **RC068** — Contemporary reporting described Widodo’s G20 priorities as global health, inclusive digital transformation, and sustainable energy, while noting that geopolitical divisions dominated the summit. Balanced portfolio evidence. **Lenses:** 8B.1, 8B.6, 8B.9. [Source](https://time.com/6232748/g20-summit-bali-geopolitical-showdown/)

- **RC069** — External analysis characterized Indonesia/ASEAN quiet diplomacy toward Myanmar as producing only limited success, while the Five-Point Consensus remained weak and violence continued. Contrary diplomatic-efficacy evidence. **Lenses:** 8B.1, 8B.6, 8B.9. [Source](https://time.com/6326274/asean-myanmar-junta-trade/)

### Disposition and handoff

- New units RC028–RC068 are proposed as `final_evidence`, subject to ledger reconciliation.
- RC039 remains `discovery_only` because the underlying page was not retrievable.
- RC063 is `unresolved`, not negative evidence.
- No evidence established personal enrichment, direct human-rights orders, command responsibility, or independently verified durable program success.
- The main remaining gaps are local-language primary records, project-level audits, regional service-quality data, direct presidential election-delay evidence, and personal/network integrity documentation.
- The workspace was read-only and shell access was blocked by the execution sandbox, so `research-materials.md` and `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be updated.
